questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arcsin\frac{4}{5}$ and $\beta=\arctan\frac{5}{12}$.
Both arguments are positive, so both angles are in quadrant 1 and every ratio is positive.
$\sin\alpha=\frac{4}{5}$ and $\cos\alpha=\frac{3}{5}$
$\sin\beta=\frac{5}{13}$ and $\cos\beta=\frac{12}{13}$
$\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta-\sin\alpha\sin\beta$
$=\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{12}{13}-\frac{4}{5}\times\frac{5}{13}$
$=\frac{36}{65}-\frac{20}{65}$
$=\frac{16}{65}$

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arccos\frac{8}{17}$, so $\cos\alpha=\frac{8}{17}$ and $\alpha$ is in quadrant 1.
$\text{opposite}=\sqrt{17^{2}-8^{2}}=15$, so $\sin\alpha=\frac{15}{17}$.
$\sin 2\alpha=2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha$
$=2\times\frac{15}{17}\times\frac{8}{17}$
$=\frac{240}{289}$

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arcsin\frac{12}{13}$ and $\beta=\arccos\frac{3}{5}$.
Both angles are in quadrant 1.
$\sin\alpha=\frac{12}{13}$ and $\cos\alpha=\frac{5}{13}$
$\cos\beta=\frac{3}{5}$ and $\sin\beta=\frac{4}{5}$
$\sin(\alpha-\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta-\cos\alpha\sin\beta$
$=\frac{12}{13}\times\frac{3}{5}-\frac{5}{13}\times\frac{4}{5}$
$=\frac{36}{65}-\frac{20}{65}$
$=\frac{16}{65}$

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arccos\left(-\frac{7}{25}\right)$, so $\cos\alpha=-\frac{7}{25}$.
$0\le\alpha\le\pi$ and $\cos\alpha<0$, so $\alpha$ is in quadrant 2.
$\text{opposite}=\sqrt{25^{2}-7^{2}}$
$=24$
The sine is positive in quadrant 2, so $\sin\alpha=\frac{24}{25}$.
$\sin 2\alpha=2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha$
$=2\times\frac{24}{25}\times\left(-\frac{7}{25}\right)$
$=-\frac{336}{625}$

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arccos\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)$, so $\cos\alpha=-\frac{2}{3}$ and $\alpha$ is in quadrant 2.
$\text{opposite}=\sqrt{3^{2}-2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$, so $\tan\alpha=-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$.
$\tan 2\alpha=\frac{2\tan\alpha}{1-\tan^{2}\alpha}$
$=\frac{-\sqrt{5}}{1-\frac{5}{4}}$
$=\frac{-\sqrt{5}}{-\frac{1}{4}}$
$=4\sqrt{5}$
